description: Discovered 2026-07-14 while building set_inlet_velocity/set_inlet_enthalpy/set_outlet_pressure BC setters for TampinesSteamArray (lateral_coupling.rs), in service of wiring TampinesSteamArray into fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube. First real exercise anywhere in the crate of step()'s pressure-velocity (PISO) coupling under a nonzero Dirichlet velocity BC -- every prior test uses default zero-gradient/passive BCs or drives he alone via set_temperature_vector. Reproduction: 10-cell, 1m pipe, 1e-4 m^2 area, dt=5e-5s (acoustically stable per dx/c_sound), pre-conditioned near 370K/1bar, then inlet velocity=0.5 m/s + inlet enthalpy=4.2e5 J/kg + outlet pressure=1e5 Pa fixed. Pressure develops a large non-physical oscillation within ~10 steps (ranging ~1e5 to ~9e5 Pa across cells against a fixed 1e5 Pa outlet BC and modest inflow -- nothing in the setup should drive a 9x pressure excursion) and panics out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range by step ~27 (see ph_flash_eqm check_if_within_ph_validity_region). Kept as an #[ignore]d regression test: openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value. Suspect the source_p boundary-flux special case for BoundaryCondition::FixedValue velocity (mod.rs step(), the 'match self.u.boundary[pi].bc' block) but not confirmed -- root-causing the PISO instability was out of scope for that session. Blocks: op-21g.6 (multiphase suite work that might build on this) is unaffected, but any consumer wanting to drive TampinesSteamArray as a prescribed-BC pipe (e.g. tampines fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube) is blocked until this is fixed.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
2026-07-14 follow-up: root-caused and fixed one real bug (phi_hbya boundary write-back missing for FixedValue velocity patches in mod.rs step() -- self.phi kept HbyA's always-zero-gradient boundary extrapolation instead of the corrected flux used in the pressure source, corrupting the next step's rhoEqn continuity). Also added the user-requested SIMPLE/PISO/PIMPLE infrastructure: get/set_n_outer_correctors, get/set_n_inner_correctors, get/set_pressure_under_relaxation, get/set_velocity_under_relaxation, and set_piso_algorithm/set_simple_algorithm/set_pimple_algorithm presets (mod.rs). With SIMPLE + heavy under-relaxation (alpha_p=0.02, alpha_u=0.3) and staying well clear of the saturation boundary, the pressure oscillation is much better behaved (bounded ~25% swing surviving 40+ iterations, vs a 9x blowup crashing by iteration 27 before the fix) but NOT fully resolved -- temperature still drifts upward and eventually exceeds the 1073.15K validity ceiling; the energy equation's stability under residual pressure noise was not root-caused. Separately (not the same run, found by moving inlet enthalpy near h_f at 1 bar): correct_thermo's (p,h) region classification and thermal_conductivity's internal (T,p) re-classification can disagree right at the saturation boundary, hitting pt_flash_eqm::cp_tp_eqm_single_phase's FwdEqnRegion::Region4 => todo!() panic -- this would block real steam-generator (boiling) use regardless of the pressure-oscillation outcome. All three findings documented in the (still #[ignore]d) regression test inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value's doc comment. Net: real progress, but wiring TampinesSteamArray into a driven steam-generator-tube use case (e.g. fhr_sim_v2) remains blocked on findings 2 and 3.
2026-07-14: FINDING 3 (saturation-boundary todo!()) RESOLVED. lambda_ph_eqm's critical-enhancement term (thermal_conductivity::lambda_2_crit_enhancement_term_tp_two_phase_estimate) delegated cp/cv/kappa_t to single-phase (T,p) routines that todo!() in region 4 (T,p not independent on the saturation line). lambda_ph_eqm calls this for EVERY region (x=0 region1, x=1 region2/3, interior region4), so the fix branches: single-phase (x==0 or x==1) keeps the exact (t,p) single-phase values bit-for-bit (verified: the 53 single-phase steam-table lambda tests that a naive t_sat-everywhere version broke now all pass again); genuine two-phase (0<x<1) quality-weights the saturated region-1/region-2 values at t_sat, mirroring cp_ph_eqm's own region-4 handling. Two new verification tests (both pass): thermal_conductivity::tests::lambda_ph_two_phase_is_finite_and_bracketed (finite, positive, bracketed by sat vapour..liquid, monotonic in quality at 1 bar) and openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::tests::correct_thermo_survives_two_phase_boiling_cell (a TampinesSteamArray cell at 1 bar / h=1.5MJ/kg / x~0.48 survives correct_thermo, T~T_sat, all fields finite). Full suite 909 passed / 0 failed. This unblocks a boiling steam-generator-tube model. Remaining on this bead: the PISO/stiff-liquid pressure-oscillation robustness (findings 1-2) for driving TampinesSteamArray hard; the source-clobber root cause (separate) is already fixed + pushed in 540fd45.
2026-07-14: TampinesSteamArray WIRED into fhr_sim_v2's steam-generator tube (secondary_loop/mod.rs), replacing the lumped h_out=h_in+Q/mdot energy balance with the spatially-resolved (p,h) steam-table physics. Persistent array (build_steam_generator_tube), driven 25 acoustic-CFL substeps per TH step, outlet enthalpy read back to feed the turbine. New standalone validation test steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater (feedwater 80degC -> boiling at 2 bar, x crosses 0 at step 5416, passes). New API set_uniform_velocity_field (pre-condition velocity to avoid water-hammer). Two integration bugs found + fixed (see tampines-steam-tables/docs/notes.md 'Correction log'): (1) default pressure floor was sat_pressure_4(273.15) EXACTLY -> clamped cells land on saturation line -> (p,h) validity guard's exact-equality Region-4 test todo!()-panics; fixed by nudging floor *1.001 into Region 1; (2) pre-init pressure (2 bar) mismatched operating outlet BC (1.2 bar) -> depressurisation rarefaction cooled a cell below 273.15K; fixed by matching pre-init to operating pressure. Live sim now runs 30s clean (0 panics), SG tube heats feedwater 90->97degC and warming. Maintainer guidance recorded: arrays use (p,h) flashing by default, not (T,p) single-phase. Remaining on this bead: the deeper stiff-liquid transient robustness (the array still panics if driven far outside its envelope, per the panic-on-out-of-range design) and enthalpy bounding as a future analogue to pressure bounding.

description:
Maintainer note, 2026-08-13 07:15 (filed outside active hours; NO search run yet -- the candidates below are from memory of the workspace layout, not from grepping).

Maintainer says a melt library is wanted, and believes one ALREADY EXISTS somewhere in this workspace. Per the search-before-building HARD RULE, step 1 is to find it, not to write one.

STEP 1 -- disambiguate what 'melt' means here. Ask the maintainer if not obvious from what turns up. At least three different things could be meant:
  (a) solid-liquid PHASE CHANGE / melting enthalpy / latent heat / mushy-zone conduction (a thermophysics feature);
  (b) CORIUM / severe-accident fuel melt and relocation (a fuel-performance / severe-accident feature);
  (c) MOLTEN SALT thermochemistry -- salt melting point, liquidus/solidus, speciation.

STEP 2 -- search candidates, in rough order of likelihood:
  - crates/outram-park-fork-thermochimica -- molten-salt Gibbs-energy minimisation, liquidus/solidus is squarely its job
  - crates/outram-park-fork-offbeat -- fuel performance, ~70 material correlations; fuel melting point very likely present
  - crates/outram-park-fork-moltres -- circulating-fuel MSR salt properties
  - crates/tampines + crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver -- solid material / thermophysics layers
  - crates/outram-foam-basic-lib -- Layer 1h thermophysics kernels
  Grep for the DOMAIN NOUN, not an intended API name: 'melt', 'melting', 'fusion', 'latent', 'liquidus', 'solidus', 'mushy', 'phase_change', 'enthalpy_of_fusion'.

STEP 3 -- report what was found and where. A checked-and-rejected answer ('X exists but does not cover Y because ...') is a good outcome and should be written back into this bead. Only if nothing covers it does new code get scoped, and then reuse > port > write.

Likely related to the conduction work in op-v9u5 (melting bounds the upper end of a conduction correlation's validity range) and to op-x0v1 (1200 C steel envelope).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
FOUND — searched 2026-08-13 by a read-only agent; every cited test was actually run and passes. Maintainer's recollection was correct.

(a) SOLID-LIQUID PHASE CHANGE -- EXISTS, VERIFIED, WIRED. Do not write another one.
  crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_options/solidification_melting.rs
    SolidificationMeltingCoefficients (:28), SolidificationMelting (:142), enthalpy-porosity method,
    Carman-Kozeny Darcy coefficient (:311), latent heat in temperature OR enthalpy form (:391).
  Two deliberate non-duplicate siblings, each documenting the boundary in its own header:
    fv_options/solidification_porosity.rs      -- tabulated Darcy blockage, no latent heat, no buoyancy
    fv_options/vof_solidification_melting.rs   -- alphaSolid(T) table capped by VoF phase fraction, no buoyancy
  Layer-5 solver: crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/melt_foam/mod.rs (MeltFoam :164), exported in prelude.rs:54.
  Tests: 31/31 fv_options, 7/7 melt_foam, 3/3 melting_vv_cases. Stefan problem vs closed-form similarity
  solution -0.035% in integrated melt thickness; energy conservation -1.27e-5%. Zero todo!().
  Known gap: the gallium cavity case is DEMONSTRATION ONLY with no reference data, and its 302.8 K
  melting point is an UNVERIFIED placeholder -- declared in tests/melting_vv_cases/References.md:52-121.

(b) CORIUM / SEVERE-ACCIDENT MELT -- GENUINELY ABSENT, and already audited.
  docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md:422 records a grep for candl|debris|rubble|corium|slump returning ZERO code hits;
  its Tier C list (:837-846) covers relocation, debris beds, molten pools, MCCI, concrete ablation. Lines 973-975
  recommend it stay OUT OF SCOPE, partly because the corium CALPHAD databases (NUCLEA etc.) are closed.
  Two false friends: offbeat/src/materials/behavioral/relocation.rs is FRAPCON cracked-fuel-fragment radial
  relocation, not core relocation; offbeat/src/materials/behavioral/phase_transition.rs:10-12 is an
  acknowledged STUB with zero public items (bead op-6sl).

(c) MOLTEN-SALT THERMOCHEMISTRY -- PARTIAL, and the working part is not where you would look.
  The real eutectic solid-liquid equilibrium is in DWSIM, not thermochimica:
    crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/thermo/flash_sle.rs -- ideal_solubility (:155),
    SleComponent::from_fusion (:208), flash_sl (:345); Schroder-van-Laar / van't Hoff; 7/7 tests pass.
  thermochimica/src/gem.rs has a 1,688-LOC minimiser but NO thermodynamic database, no liquidus/solidus surface.
  Deliberate omission to not 'fix' blindly: dwsim-libs/src/thermo/flash_single_comp.rs:46-51 intentionally omits
  every solid branch.
  Freeze margin exists only as an operational guard: fhr_sim_v2 salt_freeze_guard.rs (1,010 LOC), whose own
  docstring says the melt button 'is a cheat'.

(d) LIQUID-REGION PROPERTIES -- salts and oils yes (tuas liquid_database/: flibe, flinak, hitec, dowtherm_a,
  yd325, melting point used as the range floor). LIQUID METALS: NO.

THE ACTIONABLE GAP -- Kim 1975 and Pichler 2020 currently have NO CONSUMER.
  Zero references to kim1975 / ANL-75-55 / pichler2020 anywhere outside crates/kovan-literature/.
  1. There is NO melting-property database in the workspace. SolidificationMeltingCoefficients takes
     solidus/liquidus/latent_heat as bare f64 arguments; no Material -> (T_m, L_fus) table exists in any crate.
     Kim's T_m = 1700 K, 1670-1730 K range, 64.0 cal/g would have to be hand-typed at a call site. The melt
     SOLVER could consume it today; nothing would STORE it.
  2. There is no liquid-steel material at all, so Kim's liquid-region correlations have nowhere to live.
     ss_304_l.rs range-checks 250-1000 K (and one variant 300-700 K at :101), solid only. Offbeat's steels are
     15-15Ti and D9 cladding, not 304/316L, and carry no fusion data.

RECOMMENDATION for the maintainer: this bead is answered -- close it. The follow-on worth filing is a
melting-property store (Material -> melting point + heat of fusion, uom-typed) that the already-verified
melt solver can consume, seeded from Kim 1975. That is a genuinely new, small, well-defined piece of work,
unlike the melt library itself.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
ADDENDUM after a tracker sweep (same agent, second pass) -- corrects and sharpens the note above.

1. THE MELCOR EFFORT IS 100% PLAN, 0% CODE. No melcor/corcon crates exist; no [workspace.members] entry, not even a
   commented one; grep for melcor|corcon|contain|sparc|vanesa|cvh across all .rs/.toml returns zero real hits (only the
   substring 'contain' inside English prose). All 16 beads are Todo. op-4pw is explicit: 'THIS IS A MAINTAINER DECISION,
   not approved work: a new workspace member is not currently sanctioned anywhere in CLAUDE.md. Nothing else in the epic
   can start until this is settled.' op-acl (manual ingest) is also unstarted -- none of SAND2017-0876, SAND2017-0455,
   SAND2021-0726, NUREG/CR-6119, ML010190222 is in open/reports/.

2. CORCON / MCCI IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED EVEN FROM THE PLAN. op-exw has a section headed 'DELIBERATELY NOT FILED as
   children of this epic': MCCI/CAV deferred, blocked on closed CALPHAD databases (TAF-ID signatory-only, NUCLEA
   restricted), with the instruction not to plan around acquiring them. The epic's own target excludes source term,
   aerosols, FP transport and MCCI.

3. DOCUMENTATION HAZARD WORTH ACTING ON SEPARATELY. docs/melcor-scoping.md:80,166 calls extending thermochimica to
   corium 'the highest leverage-per-effort item in the whole list'. docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md:1126 reverses it:
   '1,479 LOC, 2 files, 6 tests, a minimiser with no database -- and the corium databases are closed. This is the single
   largest overclaim in the document.' op-qheo [P2] exists to add a correction banner and has NOT been actioned, so a
   reader landing on melcor-scoping.md today gets the overclaim with no signpost. Do not scope corium work off that file.

4. WHY THIS BEAD'S OWN CANDIDATE LIST MISSED THE ANSWER -- worth remembering. The bead admitted its candidates were
   'from memory of the workspace layout, not from grepping'. It ranked outram-foam-basic-lib LAST and never mentioned
   outram-foam-appbuilder-lib at all, which is where the solver lives. Meanwhile the workspace's own audit had already
   found it: docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md:780 lists the enthalpy-porosity melting/solidification asset explicitly.
   Reading the existing audit docs would have answered this faster than any grep.

5. CORRECTION to the 'no consumer' finding above: a consumer IS being built -- op-x0v1 (P1, in progress) is adding
   Kim's 304L SOLID-region correlations to TUAS right now. But note the ceiling gap: op-x0v1 targets 1200 degC = 1473 K,
   while Kim's melting range is 1670-1730 K. So Kim's MELTING data (T_m = 1700 K, 64.0 cal/g) and its LIQUID-region
   correlations sit above even that bead's ask and still have no home. The melting-property-store follow-on recommended
   above therefore stands, and is NOT covered by op-x0v1.

RESOLUTION: the maintainer's recollection was of BOTH a plan and an implementation, and they are different objects --
the remembered plan is the unwritten MELCOR/severe-accident epic (sense b); the implementation that actually exists is
the enthalpy-porosity melt solver (sense a). This bead is answered and can be closed.

description:
New architectural request posted to GitHub issue #35 (comment
https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/35#issuecomment-5489280039,
2026-09-01), following on from the op-9vo6 redesign checklist. Dogfooding
found that several views (Bibliography, Markdown Editor, PDF Reader) each
independently ask the user to re-select the project root/paper, and
paper-opening from Wiki/Mindmap does nothing (a stub status message).

Required: a single application-wide `active_paper: Option<ActivePaper>` on
DigitiseApp plus one `activate_paper(citekey)` operation every paper-aware
view calls into, so a root/paper is only ever selected once per session.
Full requirements, acceptance scenarios and non-goals are in the GH
comment body -- read it before starting any child of this epic.

Related: op-9vo6 (parent redesign epic, GitHub issue #35).
